parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file is in the domain layer. Its business behaviour fits that layer: the OrderStatus type, the pay() invariant that only open orders can be paid, and isPaid(). But the class also maps itself to the database. The TypeORM decorators @Entity() on class Order and @Column() on the status field define how the entity is stored and how its columns map to the schema. That is persistence work, which belongs in the infrastructure layer. In a clean split, an infrastructure repository or a separate ORM entity/schema mapping would handle it. This finding is about the mapping job the decorators do, not about which way the import points, so it falls within the rule.

violations.message: Domain class Order carries persistence mapping through TypeORM's @Entity() on the class and @Column() on the status field. ORM mapping belongs in the infrastructure layer, for example as a separate persistence entity/schema plus a repository mapper, not in the domain model.
